The Moral realism lacks adequate evidence side should identify which observations are more likely if its account is correct, which are more likely under the rival account, and what evidence would change the conclusion. Applied to the question—Are there stance-independent moral facts that people can know and that supply genuinely categorical reasons for action?—this approach replaces isolated possibility claims with a cumulative test and prevents one attractive example from carrying the entire case.

newArguments.title: Objection stress test
newArguments.text: The case can gain credibility by adopting its opponent's strongest pressure point: Treating causal contribution as the decisive test of evidence risked excluding abstract and rational knowledge before the comparison with mathematics, logic, and modality had been resolved. Rather than dismissing that concern, the side should state a specific repair, acknowledge what remains uncertain, and describe how an observer could distinguish its explanation from the leading alternatives. A conclusion that survives this stress test is stronger because it shows where the argument could fail and why the available evidence still favors it.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that mature, reasons-responsive self-government can justify bounded ordinary responsibility and proportionate accountability without requiring ultimate self-creation or metaphysically open alternatives.
premises: Responsibility-relevant control consists in stable capacities to understand reasons, foresee consequences, revise conduct, govern impulses, and act without coercion, manipulation, or disabling impairment.
These capacities are genuinely attributable to an adult when they persist across time, integrate reflection and moral learning, and are not bypassed by another controller.
Ordinary desert should mean conduct-sensitive eligibility for proportionate responses under justified public rules, not suffering valuable independently of social purposes.
A legitimate sanctioning system requires prospective justification, public notice, proportionality, due process, impairment defenses, review mechanisms, and humane limits on every imposed burden.
Within such a system, backward-looking facts about voluntary conduct can guide rule application because they identify when an agent’s protected capacities actually governed the violation.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, determinism need not defeat ordinary responsibility: suitably competent agents may be held answerable through humane, proportionate, publicly justified practices tied to their exercised capacities and conduct.

newArguments.title: The social assurance argument
newArguments.text: Accountability rules can function as reciprocal assurances among citizens who possess ordinary self-control. Each person accepts predictable constraints because others are likewise required to answer for voluntary violations, while incapacity and coercion remain defenses. This does not treat suffering as intrinsically good. It explains why conduct-sensitive responsibility can add something to generic risk management: it publicly recognizes whether a person could understand and comply with shared terms, thereby supporting equal civic standing and stable cooperation.

newArguments.title: The institutional anti-bypass principle
newArguments.text: A rule-governed system should attribute responsibility only when the agent’s deliberative capacities were part of the action-producing pathway. Manipulation, coercion, severe misinformation, and impairment reduce responsibility because they bypass or disable those capacities; deterministic causation by itself does neither. This principle converts the manipulation distinction into an administrable test and avoids claiming that agents created their own constitutions. It also explains graduated responsibility by asking how completely competent self-government participated in the specific violation.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that practical agency warrants engagement and protection, but no demonstrated feature of natural self-control independently justifies basic-desert blame or suffering.
premises: Reasons-responsive agents deliberate, learn, and modify behavior, yet their constitutive capacities and histories arise through conditions they did not ultimately select.
Adding indeterminacy cannot repair this limitation unless it supplies controlled settlement rather than introducing chance among outcomes supported by deliberation.
Protection, deterrence, rehabilitation, restitution, and moral formation can justify proportionate responses without treating suffering as deserved independently of their defensible purposes.

Forward-looking restrictions must satisfy demanding safeguards: reliable evidence, individualized necessity, equal protection, periodic review, humane conditions, and the least restrictive effective intervention.
Moral protest can communicate seriousness, recognize victims, demand repair, and set boundaries without adding the claim that an offender basically deserves hostility or suffering.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, society may preserve answerability, moral address, restitution, and necessary protection while withholding basic-desert condemnation and continuously reviewing coercive practices for necessity and fairness.

newArguments.title: The error-cost asymmetry argument
newArguments.text: Desert-based punishment can amplify institutional error because a mistaken judgment appears to authorize suffering as fitting, not merely as an unfortunate protective measure. A non-desert framework instead treats every restriction as a regrettable burden requiring continuing justification. That orientation supports review, correction, compensation, and early release when risk or evidence changes. Because criminal institutions predictably make mistakes, choosing the framework that keeps burdens presumptively contestable provides an independent reason to reject basic-desert justification.

newArguments.title: Plural replacement for moral anger
newArguments.text: No single emotion must reproduce every function attributed to moral anger. A coordinated repertoire can divide the labor: moral protest communicates condemnation, sorrow registers harm, protective resolve sets boundaries, restitution addresses victims, and sanctions prevent recurrence. This plural model answers the adult-wrongdoing objection more effectively than substituting disappointment alone. Its success should be assessed by communication, victim recognition, deterrence, reform, and relational repair, allowing empirical comparison without presupposing that hostile anger is uniquely fitting.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that some human choices may be genuinely free when an integrated agent rationally settles among live alternatives for reasons without antecedent conditions uniquely necessitating the settlement.
premises: A libertarian claim need establish only that genuinely available alternatives occur in some suitably reflective decisions, not that every action, impulse, impairment, or habit is free.
An agent can be biologically and environmentally embedded while retaining control unless those influences are shown to uniquely necessitate which supported alternative becomes actual.
Reasons may guide a selection without necessitating it when the choice expresses the agent’s evaluative perspective, remains intelligible, and is settled through the agent’s deliberative activity.

The appearance of such control supplies defeasible evidence when coherently integrated with deliberation, but its weight must vary with impairment, manipulation, predictive success, and contrary mechanistic evidence.

Even if genuine control sometimes exists, responsibility should track the quality of alternatives, understanding, coercion, impairment, and reasons-responsiveness rather than license unrestricted retribution.
finalArgument.conclusion: Accordingly, pervasive causal influence does not by itself eliminate the possibility that some reflective choices are reason-guided settlements attributable to agents and capable of grounding carefully limited responsibility.

newArguments.title: Contrastive intervention test
newArguments.text: A useful empirical program would compare decisions under matched reasons while experimentally varying coercion, cognitive impairment, attentional disruption, and opportunities for reflective reconsideration. If agent-level deliberative capacities systematically explain contrastive differences beyond coarse antecedent predictors, that would not prove libertarian freedom, but it would identify the precise control phenomenon requiring explanation. The pro case could then avoid relying entirely on undifferentiated intuition and instead argue that a successful theory must preserve the causal and normative significance of integrated reflective agency.

newArguments.title: The authorship luck filter
newArguments.text: The strongest libertarian model should impose a luck filter: an undetermined outcome counts as free only when it issues from stable evaluative commitments, competent awareness, reasons that favor the act, and a deliberative mechanism owned by the person. Mere neural noise or quantum variation would fail these conditions. This framework directly answers the randomness objection by making indeterminacy necessary at most, never sufficient, and locating authorship in the structured relation among agent, reasons, capacities, and settlement.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that human conduct arises through causally continuous biological and environmental processes, so responsibility should regulate behavior humanely without presuming ultimate self-origination or basic retributive desert.
premises: Every observed decision depends upon neural states and capacities shaped by physiology, development, learning, social context, inherited traits, and immediate environmental inputs.
When relevant antecedent conditions change through learning, treatment, incentives, trauma, fatigue, or altered information, behavior predictably changes through the same causally embedded organism.

Libertarian sourcehood requires more than reasons-responsiveness because the agent’s evaluative character, weighing process, and capacity to settle are themselves products of conditions the agent did not ultimately choose.

Introducing an undetermined selection does not create authorship unless a further account explains how the person controls that variation, and any such account must avoid merely relocating prior causation.

Protection, rehabilitation, deterrence, restitution, and moral communication can remain justified as causal interventions, while proportionality and rights forbid sacrificing innocent people for aggregate behavioral effects.
finalArgument.conclusion: Accordingly, the evidence supports rejecting ultimate self-created authorship and basic retributive desert while retaining bounded, rights-respecting practices that causally protect people and improve future conduct.

newArguments.title: The sourcehood regress
newArguments.text: Suppose a reflective agent settles a choice by endorsing one reason over another. The con case can ask what explains the evaluative standards, attention, memory, emotional weighting, and deliberative capacity producing that endorsement. If those features arise from prior biology and experience, the settlement lacks ultimate self-origination; if they arise without explanation, their unexplained occurrence adds no ownership. This regress does not show that deliberation is unreal, but it challenges the stronger claim that deliberation makes an agent the ultimate source required for basic desert.

newArguments.title: Rights-respecting quarantine model
newArguments.text: A nonretributive system can distinguish offender from innocent person through evidence, causal responsibility for harm, due process, proportional risk management, and strict rights against instrumental sacrifice. The justification resembles quarantine: restriction may be permissible to prevent serious harm, but imposed suffering is not valuable because anyone deserves pain. This answers the framing objection without appealing to ultimate desert, since framing lacks causal responsibility, violates rights, corrupts institutions, and predictably increases insecurity while offering no legitimate individualized basis for restraint.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that irreducibility is warranted only if indispensable first-person, normative, and agentive facts cannot be captured by any complete realization account, not merely because microphysical vocabulary omits them.
premises: Any adequate account must explain why there is a determinate first-person perspective, not only why a system reports, discriminates, integrates, and acts upon information.
Systematic brain dependence is compatible with production, constitution, filtering, or realization, so metaphysical conclusions require evidence that discriminates among those relations.
Normative reasons purport to justify conduct, and a complete theory must explain their authority as well as the causal history through which agents acquire moral practices.
A freedom theory must explain an agent's ownership of deliberation and control, while avoiding both antecedent compulsion and an uncontrolled random selection among outcomes.
Explanatory pluralism alone does not decide ontology; the decisive question is whether realization relations preserve every causal, experiential, and normative feature without remainder.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, a limited case for irreducibility remains reasonable where a specified experiential, normative, or agentive feature survives the strongest available realization account, although no blanket rejection of naturalistic explanation follows.

newArguments.title: Contrastive realization test
newArguments.text: A stronger pro methodology would compare rival realization theories using contrastive cases. If two systems share every proposed functional, behavioral, computational, and relational property, the pro side should ask whether the theories nevertheless permit a difference in experience, normative authority, or ownership. If they do, the realization base is incomplete by the theory's own lights; if they do not, the pro side can demand an explanation of why the identity is necessary rather than stipulated. This test converts a general intuition about irreducibility into a focused burden for competing accounts.

newArguments.title: Normative error constraint
newArguments.text: A naturalized value account must explain not only agreement and improvement within practices but also the possibility that an entire settled practice is unjust. The pro side can argue that practice-independent standards earn explanatory work when they make systematic moral error intelligible without reducing error to inconsistency with another local convention. This does not establish a supernatural source of value; it instead places a precise adequacy constraint on constructivist theories and leaves open several realist ontologies compatible with the limited irreducibility thesis.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that materially realized organization can explain persons when it accounts for experience-related capacities, diachronic selfhood, purpose, normativity, and responsible control at their appropriate levels without positing causally idle additions.
premises: Neural interventions systematically alter awareness, memory, personality, and control, making brain realization the evidential default while leaving metaphysical conclusions defeasible.
An evolved self-model can integrate perception, memory, prediction, and action without a second inner observer, provided the account distinguishes useful representation from denial of experience.

Natural selection, learning, and culture can successively generate biological functions, individual goals, and socially assessable reasons even though elementary physical regularities have no purposes.
Moral practices can be constructed yet objectively improvable relative to facts about agency, suffering, cooperation, consistency, and the consequences of alternative institutional arrangements.
Responsibility can track reasons-responsive self-control, learning capacity, and freedom from coercive external management rather than identical-past alternatives or random physical variation.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, naturalism can provisionally explain persons through empirically grounded realization and autonomous higher-level descriptions, while remaining answerable to unresolved questions about phenomenal character, normativity, and ownership of agency.

newArguments.title: Intervention convergence argument
newArguments.text: Naturalism gains support when independently targeted interventions converge on the same organized capacities. Changes to neural circuitry, development, learning environments, and social scaffolding can each alter memory continuity, purposive planning, moral sensitivity, and self-control in predictable ways. Convergence would be difficult to explain if the decisive personal properties belonged primarily to an independent subject whose relation to these interventions remained unspecified. The inference is defeasible, but it gives naturalism a comparative evidential advantage and identifies what an irreducibility theory must explain rather than relying solely on methodological optimism.

newArguments.title: Cross-level causal stability
newArguments.text: Higher-level properties earn realism when they support stable counterfactuals across many physical implementations. A promise, goal, belief, or autonomous policy can explain behavior even when its neural details vary, because changing the higher-level state would predictably change action across realizations. Naturalism can therefore preserve causal significance without requiring fundamental particles to contain promises or purposes. This answers the catalogue objection more directly than simple analogy: explanatory autonomy reflects robust organization and counterfactual structure, while metaphysical addition would require separate evidence beyond the usefulness of the higher-level description.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that analytic idealism is preferable when consciousness is treated as intrinsic reality and physical structure as its relational description, provided the theory earns its advantage through explicit constraints on boundaries, causation, and shared observation.
premises: Experience is directly instantiated, whereas a wholly nonexperiential intrinsic substrate is theoretically posited; an ontology that begins with instantiated experience therefore avoids one category transition, although that consideration establishes only an initial parsimony advantage.

Physical theories principally specify relational, quantitative, and causal structure, so analytic idealism may interpret that successful structure as the public description of intrinsically experiential processes without rejecting any validated scientific prediction.

Observer independence requires independence from individual observers, not independence from every possible form of mentality; external universal processes can therefore constrain multiple perspectives and support stable intersubjective correction.

Dissociative boundaries should be modeled as dynamically maintained restrictions on reciprocal informational and causal access, allowing the proposal to distinguish local perspectives without treating metaphorical dissociation as a complete mechanism.

Intrinsic dispositions must be constrained by empirically recoverable symmetries, conservation relations, and transition rules, so universal subjectivity does not explain order merely by being assigned unspecified powers.
finalArgument.conclusion: Analytic idealism deserves conditional preference only if its experiential intrinsic basis reproduces scientific structure, yields testable boundary conditions, and explains differentiated causation with fewer unsupported primitives than neutral or nonexperiential competitors.

newArguments.title: Constraint-equivalence research program
newArguments.text: Analytic idealism can convert a metaphysical proposal into a research program by requiring every successful physical constraint to have an isomorphic formulation in terms of experiential dynamics. Failure to recover a conservation law, symmetry, or intervention pattern would count against the idealist model rather than being absorbed by metaphor. This does not independently prove mentality fundamental, but it makes the view comparatively assessable and directly answers the objection that labeling the substrate mental contributes no explanatory discipline.

newArguments.title: Boundary degradation predictions
newArguments.text: If individual subjects are dynamically restricted regions within a wider experiential process, then graded changes in integration and reciprocal access should predict systematic changes in perspective, memory ownership, and cross-boundary influence. The relevant evidence would not establish universal consciousness by itself, but convergent boundary signatures could distinguish a disciplined dissociation model from an unrestricted metaphor. This strengthens the account by stating what successful individuation would require and by permitting observations to disfavor particular implementations.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that neutral monism should remain the preferred restraint position until either idealism or physicalism explains why structured representations are phenomenal, because rejecting emergence does not determine the intrinsic nature of the neutral basis.
premises: The failure of a proposed derivation from physical quantities to experiential qualities underdetermines ontology, since idealist, dual-aspect, neutral, and primitive-law accounts remain logically available and require comparative assessment.

Representations can be characterized minimally as states whose causal role systematically tracks, compresses, and guides action concerning other states, without initially deciding whether their intrinsic bearer is mental or physical.

Phenomenality should be attributed only where a representational process has integrated perspective-sensitive availability, counterfactual coherence, and temporally organized access, avoiding indiscriminate experience attribution to every informational state.

Any ontology must explain predictive organization, boundaries, and differentiated causation; naming the intrinsic substrate mental, physical, or neutral cannot substitute for models that yield those structures and intervention patterns.

Selfless dreams and altered states indicate that autobiographical self-representation, ordinary spacetime organization, and phenomenal presence can vary independently, providing comparative constraints without directly settling metaphysical fundamentality.
finalArgument.conclusion: Neutral monism is warranted as a provisional framework if it specifies representation and phenomenality more precisely, applies equal explanatory standards to itself, and withholds claims about intrinsic substance until comparative evidence favors one interpretation.

newArguments.title: Multiple intrinsic realizations
newArguments.text: Suppose identical relational and representational organization could be described consistently under mental, physical, or neutral intrinsic vocabularies while generating the same predictions. Then current evidence would not select among those intrinsic interpretations, and ontological restraint would be rationally preferable to premature identification. This argument does not show that every interpretation is equally adequate; it establishes a concrete selection burden requiring evidence that discriminates intrinsic nature rather than merely confirming shared structure.

newArguments.title: Perturbational phenomenal profiles
newArguments.text: A neutral representational theory could earn content by predicting how interventions alter perspective-sensitive availability, temporal coherence, self-modeling, and reported phenomenal differentiation. Instead of equating integration with consciousness, it would compare multidimensional perturbational profiles across waking, dreaming, meditative, and disrupted states. The proposal remains neutral about intrinsic substance, but it creates empirical conditions under which particular accounts of phenomenal representation can succeed or fail and directly answers the complaint that neutrality merely postpones explanation.

finalArgument.thesis: The strongest cautious case is that current origin-of-life research has demonstrated intriguing chemical mechanisms but has not yet experimentally connected them into a heritable, metabolically sustained, evolvable system warranting claims of substantial explanatory proximity.
premises: Evidence for simple early chemistry and later cellular life identifies endpoints but does not itself supply the mechanisms connecting molecular production, compartmentalization, metabolism, heredity, and cumulative selection.

Autocatalysis, templating, or high molecular complexity can be relevant intermediate achievements without being sufficient evidence of sustained replication, selectable variation, or integrated cellular organization.

Operational claims about metabolism and self-replication require measured persistence, copying fidelity, heredity, and functionality under controls that exclude externally maintained or transient reaction cycles.

A warranted overstatement finding should compare identifiable communications with the actual experimental results and mark precisely where possibility, demonstrated mechanism, and integrated pathway are being conflated.
finalArgument.conclusion: Accordingly, substantial proximity should be asserted only when experiments connect multiple stages under shared conditions and satisfy published heredity, persistence, fidelity, and functional-selection criteria; until then, narrower mechanism-specific claims are better supported.

newArguments.title: Interface compatibility burden
newArguments.text: Even individually successful origin experiments may not compose into a pathway because their products, solvents, temperatures, concentrations, energy sources, and purification requirements can be mutually incompatible. A stronger assessment of proximity should therefore evaluate interfaces: whether the output of one stage becomes the usable input of the next without investigator redesign or destructive environmental switching. Demonstrating several isolated mechanisms is weaker than demonstrating a chemically continuous sequence, and this distinction supplies a concrete way to test whether a research program has crossed from a catalog of possibilities to an integrated pathway.

newArguments.title: Error-threshold accounting
newArguments.text: A copying system can contribute to cumulative evolution only if its fidelity, population size, resource flow, and degradation rate jointly preserve enough heritable structure for selection to act. Rather than demanding modern biological accuracy, the pro case can ask researchers to publish an error budget for each proposed precursor. That budget would identify how much information survives each generation and whether advantageous variants persist longer than chemical noise. This makes the fidelity objection quantitative and avoids treating either one successful copy or one imperfect primitive replicator as decisive by itself.

finalArgument.thesis: The strongest emerging-pathway case is that progress consists not in reproducing Earth's exact history or already making a cell, but in experimentally discovering measurable, composable mechanisms that generate organization, copying, variation, and selection from simpler chemistry.
premises: Scientific explanation can establish lawful generative possibility and constrain classes of pathways even when historical evidence cannot identify the unique molecular sequence followed on early Earth.

Coupled catalytic sets and templated molybdate organization are relevant because they demonstrate nontrivial network behavior from comparatively simple inputs, not because they already constitute cellular life.

Syntactic information and objective molecular complexity can become useful transition measures if operational definitions, controls, and prospective predictions distinguish organized chemical causation from rarity alone.

Permissive laboratory environments can test whether primitive copying and selection arise without prescribing the sequence, provided experiments vary conditions transparently and measure sustained heredity and functional change.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, current work can reasonably be described as an emerging testable pathway when it yields reproducible mechanisms and risky predictions across successive stages, while claims of a completed historical or cellular explanation remain premature.

newArguments.title: Convergent pathway evidence
newArguments.text: Historical uniqueness need not prevent strong inference if chemically different starting conditions repeatedly converge on the same functional motifs. Researchers could vary minerals, energy sources, wet-dry cycles, and precursor mixtures, then ask whether comparable catalytic networks, compartments, or copying behaviors emerge. Convergence would support the existence of robust generative principles rather than a laboratory-specific curiosity; divergence would constrain the theory. This approach produces risky comparative predictions and turns uncertainty about Earth's exact sequence into an experimental design advantage instead of an excuse for unconstrained storytelling.

newArguments.title: Milestone graph validation
newArguments.text: The emerging-pathway claim can be tested with a directed milestone graph rather than a single leap from chemistry to cells. Nodes would represent measured capacities such as templating, compartment persistence, resource coupling, copying, heritable variation, and adaptive improvement; edges would require experiments showing that one capacity enables the next under compatible conditions. Failed edges would identify genuine gaps, while repeated successful edges would establish cumulative progress without pretending that the entire route is complete. This framework directly accommodates the opponent's threshold demands while preserving the evidential value of partial mechanisms.

finalArgument.thesis: The strongest dualist case is that unified first-person consciousness supplies defeasible evidence for a nonphysical subject, whose persistence is possible if identity belongs to that subject rather than its presently operative capacities.
premises: Complete third-person descriptions appear to leave open which determinate phenomenal character is instantiated, while first-person acquaintance supplies information that excludes experiential alternatives.
A person's simultaneously integrated rational, sensory, emotional, and phenomenal states require one bearer, although unity alone does not yet determine whether that bearer is physical.

If phenomenal character and intrinsic intentional content resist exhaustive functional characterization, the hypothesis of a nonphysical bearer gains comparative support rather than following deductively.

Dependence of thought and action on neural integrity establishes conditions for present operation, but it does not by itself decide whether the underlying subject ceases to exist when those conditions disappear.
A defensible survival claim requires a nonarbitrary continuity relation, such as direct causal persistence of the same subject, rather than mere resemblance or recurrence of a duplicate.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, if the comparative explanatory case for a nonphysical bearer succeeds and direct subject-level continuity is coherent, bodily death need not entail that person's nonexistence, although actual survival requires further evidence.

newArguments.title: Causal continuity without duplication
newArguments.text: A survival theory should not identify a future person merely by resemblance, because resemblance can be duplicated and therefore cannot uniquely select one continuer. The dualist can instead propose that numerical identity follows an unbroken causal history of the subject itself: the same bearer first supports embodied capacities, later lacks operative capacities, and may subsequently support capacities in another organism. This does not demonstrate that such histories occur, but it gives the reembodiment proposal a determinate identity condition and prevents arbitrary cross-species assignments.

newArguments.title: Comparative explanatory risk
newArguments.text: Naturalism and dualism face different explanatory risks. Naturalism must show how multiscale organization yields determinate phenomenal character and original intentional content; dualism must show how a nonphysical subject interacts with brains and persists across disembodiment. The dualist case becomes stronger if it presents these as comparative research burdens rather than treating present naturalistic incompleteness as proof. Evidence that phenomenal or intentional explanations repeatedly require first-person or semantic primitives would then count modestly for a nonphysical bearer, while remaining open to future naturalistic improvement.

finalArgument.thesis: The strongest naturalist case is that persons are unified organisms whose mental properties operate at biological and psychological scales, while no independent evidence requires an additional bearer capable of surviving neural destruction.
premises: Naturalism need not reduce every legitimate property to microphysical vocabulary, because organized systems possess scale-specific properties with stable causal and explanatory roles.

Experiential knowledge may require occupying the relevant physical state, so Mary's new perspective is compatible with learning through a new epistemic route rather than discovering another substance.

Intentional content and reason-responsive agency can be grounded in organism-level functions that track environments, guide correction, and integrate beliefs with deliberation across changing circumstances.

Systematic covariation between neural integrity and every evidenced personal capacity supports identifying the person with the functioning organism, even though correlation alone does not prove that no inactive bearer exists.
A surviving subject with no independently detectable properties, activities, memories, or continuity conditions adds no established explanatory work beyond the organismic account of the evidence.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, the available argumentative structure favors treating conscious persons as natural organisms and withholding belief in postmortem personal survival unless independent evidence identifies a persisting bearer and its continuity conditions.

newArguments.title: Intervention profile of personhood
newArguments.text: Competing identity theories should predict the effects of targeted interventions. On the organismic view, altering memory systems, attention networks, affective regulation, or executive control should selectively alter corresponding aspects of the person, while preserving capacities supported elsewhere. That structured intervention profile is what a distributed biological system predicts. A soul theory can accommodate the same findings by treating the brain as an interface, but without independent constraints it risks matching every possible result. Predictive restrictions therefore provide a comparative reason to prefer organismic identity while stopping short of proving that no soul exists.

newArguments.title: Evidence required for identity
newArguments.text: Numerical identity across a discontinuity requires evidence that distinguishes one alleged continuer from every qualitatively identical candidate. Bodily and psychological continuity offer public causal relations that can perform this selecting role. A wholly inactive soul, by contrast, is stipulated to manifest no memory, disposition, action, or measurable connection during disembodiment. Unless the theory supplies another constrained relation, later embodiment cannot be identified as continuation rather than replacement. This evidential underdetermination weakens reincarnation claims independently of whether nonphysical subjects are conceptually possible or whether cosmic recurrence occurs.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that natural sufficiency is best defended as a cumulative, experimentally constrained research hypothesis whose mechanisms explain different stages without claiming that every transition has already been reconstructed.
premises: Independent experimental successes involving precursor formation, polymers, catalytic RNA-related chemistry, and fatty-acid compartments raise the plausibility of a staged natural pathway even when complete integration remains unresolved.

Endosymbiosis demonstrates that major increases in cellular organization can result from historically contingent incorporation and subsequent coordination of previously autonomous biological components.

Selection and exaptation can accumulate functional organization once heredity and differential persistence exist, but their application to life's earliest stages must specify the relevant replicating context.

A fair comparison should ask which program generates tractable experiments, constrained intermediate hypotheses, and converging evidence, rather than treating either current gaps or future possibilities as decisive.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, natural processes remain a proportionate sufficient-framework hypothesis when supported stage by stage, although unresolved integration prevents claiming a complete historical reconstruction of life's origin.

newArguments.title: Convergent constraint mapping
newArguments.text: A natural-origin program gains strength when independent lines of chemistry constrain the same sequence rather than merely producing isolated ingredients. Researchers could preregister compatibility requirements for temperature, salinity, energy sources, concentrations, catalytic surfaces, membrane stability, and molecular persistence, then test whether proposed stages occupy overlapping environmental ranges. Convergence would answer the integration objection more directly than a catalogue of separate successes; failure would identify where the framework requires revision. This creates a risky, cumulative evidential structure without pretending that an incomplete pathway is already complete.

newArguments.title: Nested continuity predictions
newArguments.text: If cellular complexity arose cumulatively, modern systems should preserve nested traces of earlier workable arrangements: homologous modules, redundant pathways, co-opted components, historical constraints, and intermediates whose partial functions remain selectable. Endosymbiosis already illustrates this reasoning at one level, but the steelman would apply it prospectively across translation, membranes, and metabolic networks. The strength of the natural account would depend on multiple independent continuity predictions succeeding together, not on any single resemblance. This approach also distinguishes evolutionary reuse from a generic appeal to natural processes.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that intelligent agency should be considered only if a specified agency model predicts a coordinated evidential pattern substantially less expected under the strongest natural alternatives.
premises: Origin scenarios must satisfy simultaneous constraints involving polymer formation, catalysis, environmental compatibility, compartmentalization, heredity, and integration rather than solving each requirement under unrelated conditions.

Future discoveries may reasonably guide research, but present sufficiency claims require independently supported mechanisms with properties adequate for the specific catalytic and organizational tasks assigned to them.

Laboratory agency becomes historically relevant only when investigators contribute organization that environmental processes demonstrably cannot reproduce, not merely when experiments require control and measurement.
A scientific agency model must specify risky outcomes, possible falsifiers, and evidence ratios comparing intervention with natural evolutionary and chemical alternatives.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, agency merits consideration as a conditional scientific hypothesis only where specified predictions outperform natural alternatives; unresolved natural pathways alone do not establish that condition.

newArguments.title: Intervention signature matrix
newArguments.text: An agency model could preregister a matrix of predicted signatures rather than appeal generally to engineering resemblance. Candidate signatures might include abrupt coordinated dependencies lacking functional precursors, unusually concentrated sequence solutions, modular interfaces optimized for multiple future contexts, and patterns inconsistent with accessible chemical or selective trajectories. Each signature would require an explicit natural baseline and a stated falsifier. No single feature would settle the inference, but a convergent pattern could provide genuinely comparative evidence while repeated natural-pathway discoveries would weaken the agency model.

newArguments.title: Joint feasibility burden
newArguments.text: The strongest chemical objection is not that individual prebiotic reactions never occur, but that a historical pathway must join them without mutually destructive conditions. A rigorous con case would define a joint-feasibility model covering concentrations, timescales, energy inputs, side reactions, molecular stability, compartment permeability, and transfer between environments. It would then test published pathways against the same criteria. Persistent incompatibility across revised models would strengthen the insufficiency case, whereas demonstrated compatibility would count against it. This converts broad declarations of intractability into a revisable empirical research program.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that meaningful scientific proximity requires an integrated, environmentally credible reaction network whose measurable progress exceeds its competing losses.
premises: Component synthesis bears on origin only to the extent that products persist, remain mutually compatible, and become available to subsequent stages under connected environmental conditions.
Formation rates must be evaluated together with degradation, dilution, side reactions, replenishment, concentration, and retention in the same environmental model.
Opportunity-space reasoning becomes informative only after a candidate model defines an eligible trial, its conditional transitions, and the dependencies linking its stages.
A pathway can be assessed incrementally through predefined milestones without treating either an isolated synthesis as completion or incomplete integration as proof of impossibility.
finalArgument.conclusion: Accordingly, present evidence should count as meaningful proximity only where linked experiments demonstrate net accumulation, compatible transitions, and increasing system-level organization under plausible conditions.

newArguments.title: Integrated net-flux benchmark
newArguments.text: An origin pathway should be evaluated as a connected reaction network rather than as a catalog of individually successful syntheses. For each proposed environment, researchers would measure production, degradation, dilution, concentration, retention, and transfer into later stages. A network counts as advancing only when useful intermediates accumulate or recycle faster than they disappear and when the conditions supporting one stage do not disable the next. This benchmark makes the continuity objection testable and permits direct comparison among hydrothermal, surface-cycling, mineral-assisted, and compartmentalized scenarios.

newArguments.title: Prospective milestone ledger
newArguments.text: Before interpreting new experiments, proponents and critics could publish shared milestones for pathway progress: environmentally available precursors, selective accumulation, compatible multistep transfer, functional coupling, bounded heredity, and sustained adaptive improvement. Each milestone would identify the observation that satisfies it and the failure that weakens it. Prospective criteria would prevent publicity around a component synthesis from being mistaken for a completed pathway, while also preventing every partial result from being dismissed merely because life has not been produced. The resulting ledger would make claims about an approaching or receding target empirically auditable.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is structured agnosticism: incomplete mechanism does not erase graded evidence, but every confidence update should be tied to explicit experiments, searches, and selection controls.
premises: Controlled experiments can establish bounded causal capacities and environmental constraints even when they do not reproduce a continuous historical pathway.
Repeated independent origins would update natural accessibility only after shared ancestry, transfer, contamination, and direct intervention are addressed by the evidentiary design.
Nondetection bears on rarity only in proportion to the number of eligible environments searched, detection sensitivity, biosignature persistence, and independence tests.
Possibility claims should distinguish physical allowance, demonstrated component chemistry, integrated pathway plausibility, historical frequency, and confidence in a particular reconstruction.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, the warranted position is neither a completed natural-origin account nor a declaration of chemical failure, but calibrated updating across explicitly separated evidentiary levels.

newArguments.title: Graded evidence ladder
newArguments.text: Origin evidence can be organized into levels: physically permitted reactions, demonstrated component formation, compatible multistep chemistry, persistent self-maintaining networks, bounded heredity, and independently arisen natural life. Evidence at one level does not automatically establish the next, but neither is it worthless because the complete ladder remains unclimbed. Reporting which level an experiment reaches, which assumptions connect it upward, and which observations could reverse the update would give limited clues disciplined evidentiary weight. This framework answers the pathway objection without misrepresenting partial laboratory results as a historical reconstruction.

newArguments.title: Detection-power calibration
newArguments.text: The evidential meaning of extraterrestrial life depends upon the search process, not merely the number of positive detections. Investigators should report the population of eligible environments, detection sensitivity, biosignature lifetime, contamination controls, transfer pathways, and tests of biochemical independence. Positive cases could then update accessibility through an explicit likelihood model, while nondetections would update rarity only according to actual search power. This asymmetric treatment prevents one discovery from mechanically settling mechanism and prevents an observationally weak silence from being treated as strong evidence that origin is singular or scientifically inaccessible.

finalArgument.thesis: The strongest metaphorical account holds that historical inquiry can affirm Jesus's kingdom-centered, nonviolent mission while treating resurrection primarily as communal participation in God's vindication, without claiming that this interpretation disproves every bodily reading.
premises: Gospel redaction and known Synoptic dependence require historians to distinguish the number of narratives from the number of demonstrably independent evidentiary streams.
Jesus's historically recoverable emphasis on God's present kingdom and communal participation supplies a coherent center for interpreting later claims about his identity and vindication.

Pauline and narrative bodily language must be acknowledged as evidence, yet its existence alone does not settle source independence, genre, historical occurrence, or the exact continuity involved in transformation.

A resurrection interpretation earns historical and theological credibility when it explains the disciples' continuing allegiance, transformed communal practices, and proclamation of divine vindication together.

Because bodily occurrence and communal significance are logically compatible, the metaphorical case should claim interpretive priority only where its source analysis and explanatory reach provide comparative support.
finalArgument.conclusion: Accordingly, a historically cautious reader may reasonably prefer participatory vindication as the best-supported organizing interpretation while remaining agnostic about whether an additional bodily event occurred.

newArguments.title: Explanatory layering test
newArguments.text: Instead of asking whether resurrection language is either literal or metaphorical, compare interpretations across distinct explanatory layers: what event the sources report, how communities interpreted it, and what practices the interpretation produced. A bodily proposal may address the first layer, while participatory vindication may explain the latter two more fully. The metaphorical case becomes stronger when it shows that its account explains durable communal transformation without pretending that practical consequences alone determine event mechanics.

newArguments.title: Dependence-sensitive convergence
newArguments.text: Convergence should be weighted by demonstrated independence rather than by document count. Synoptic dependence lowers the incremental force of repeated narrative details, while distinct Pauline material may retain separate weight even if it differs in genre and purpose. This approach neither dismisses the sources nor assumes their full independence. It gives the metaphorical route a principled method for explaining why multiple attestations can remain historically significant without automatically yielding several independent confirmations of identical bodily mechanics.

finalArgument.thesis: The strongest bodily-resurrection account argues that early, partly independent testimony makes transformed embodiment historically preferable to an exclusively metaphorical explanation, while leaving supernatural causation and detailed resurrection mechanics beyond the historical conclusion.
premises: Historical reconstruction is necessarily partial, but disciplined criteria can still compare explanations when their factual preconditions and limitations are explicitly defended.
Paul's coordination of Christ's raising with believers' transformed bodies provides significant evidence that early resurrection proclamation exceeded changed behavior or communal survival alone.
Mark, John, and Paul can contribute cumulative evidence only to the degree that their relevant traditions, literary relationships, and physical claims are independently established.
The Gospel raising narratives plainly depict literal deaths and restorations, demonstrating that theological significance and literal narrative assertion can coexist within the same account.
Historical affirmation of an extraordinary event need not identify its supernatural cause, but it must compare rarity, source quality, dependence, and alternative explanations transparently.
finalArgument.conclusion: Accordingly, transformed bodily resurrection may be judged the preferable historical explanation if source-level independence and comparative explanatory superiority are established, without claiming historical proof of divine causation.

newArguments.title: Incremental-source matrix
newArguments.text: Evaluate Mark, John, and Paul in a matrix separating date, literary dependence, tradition-level independence, genre, and exact bodily content. Each source then contributes only its incremental evidentiary value rather than receiving an all-or-nothing label of independent witness. If Paul independently supplies transformed embodiment and a Gospel independently supplies tomb or appearance material, their convergence can be specified without exaggeration. This framework makes the bodily case more resilient because its cumulative force becomes inspectable at the level actually disputed.

newArguments.title: Meaning without displacement
newArguments.text: The ethical force emphasized by the metaphorical account can be incorporated rather than opposed: a bodily resurrection could function as divine vindication of nonviolent resistance and generate participatory communal transformation. This removes a false competitive pressure between event and significance. The bodily case should then argue comparatively that physical transformation explains why bodily language persisted, while Crossan's political and communal themes explain what the event meant. Such integration answers the strongest pro insight without treating meaningful metaphor as evidence against occurrence.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that a carefully specified personal-creator hypothesis may receive cumulative support when simplicity, purposive intelligibility, consciousness, moral agency, and cosmic regularity are assessed together under explicit evidential constraints.
premises: Intentional explanation is indispensable in ordinary reasoning because an agent's goals, information, and capacities can explain action patterns that a bare physical description does not explanatory-select by itself.

Simplicity should influence prior plausibility only among sufficiently specified hypotheses whose observable implications remain compatible with the evidence and whose complexity is assessed under declared criteria.

A good creator could have convergent reasons for stable laws, embodied rational agents, discoverable regularities, and environments permitting cooperative action, although those reasons generate ranges rather than precise outcomes.

Consciousness may remain evidentially relevant if rival hypotheses differ in how naturally they accommodate first-person subjects, even when physical and evolutionary accounts explain embodiment and behavioral capacities.

Any morally adequate theism must treat severe suffering as genuine counterevidence and require victim-centered reasons, restoration, continuing agency, and constraints preventing appeals to aggregate goods from overriding individuals.
finalArgument.conclusion: Accordingly, theism can remain a serious cumulative explanatory candidate if its divine attributes, simplicity metric, qualitative expectations, and victim-centered moral constraints are independently specified and comparatively tested.

newArguments.title: Cross-domain compression test
newArguments.text: A creator hypothesis should be evaluated by whether one independently motivated character description compresses several domains without acquiring separate adjustable clauses for each observation. Stable laws, rational knowers, moral interaction, and consciousness would count together only if the same divine attributes generate them and also exclude meaningful alternatives. This test answers the non-specificity objection by penalizing post hoc preference additions. It also gives the simplicity claim an operational target: not verbal brevity alone, but explanatory compression constrained by observable consequences.

newArguments.title: Protected agency principle
newArguments.text: A stronger freedom defense would distinguish ordinary risk from agency-annihilating harm. If valuable freedom is the aim, conditions that permanently prevent a person from developing agency require a special justification and cannot be defended merely by another person's choices. Theism could therefore predict moral limits, opportunities for continued development, and direct divine obligations toward each victim. This does not erase the evidential force of suffering, but it converts the reply from generic compensation into a structured principle that can be tested against the hardest cases.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that theism has not earned comparative preference unless its simplicity measure, causal model, predictive constraints, and moral implications outperform relevant alternatives rather than merely remaining compatible with observed reality.
premises: Descriptive brevity, ontological economy, computational tractability, and parameter economy can rank hypotheses differently, so a simplicity advantage requires a declared metric and principled aggregation rule.

A personal explanation drawn from embodied agents receives weaker background support when extended to instantaneous bodiless causation unless a connecting model explains the analogy's relevant similarities.
A hypothesis gains evidential support through observations only when those observations are more expected under it than under relevant rivals, not merely because it can accommodate them afterward.

Evolutionary and physical explanations already account for substantial portions of order, embodiment, adaptation, and behavior, so remaining explanatory gaps must be isolated rather than credited with the entire package.
Severe suffering is especially resistant to generic freedom or compensation replies when it predictably destroys the victim's agency, development, relationships, and embodied opportunities.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, withholding comparative preference for theism is warranted until a specified divine hypothesis supplies defensible complexity measures, discriminating expectations, causal coherence, and an adequate victim-centered account of suffering.

newArguments.title: Predictive budget requirement
newArguments.text: Grant each hypothesis a limited predictive budget: every independent auxiliary assumption used to fit an observation consumes part of its simplicity advantage. A creator theory that separately adds preferences for laws, life, embodiment, hiddenness, suffering, and an afterlife may be descriptively short while functionally parameter-rich. The comparison should therefore record which outcomes follow from the core hypothesis, which require added moral principles, and which remain unconstrained. This framework turns non-specificity into a transparent accounting problem rather than a dispute over rhetorical elegance.

newArguments.title: Opportunity-loss evidence
newArguments.text: Harms should be evaluated not only by experienced pain or total lifetime welfare but also by destroyed option sets. Premature death can eliminate education, relationships, moral development, projects, and choices that later benefits cannot make historically available. Even if continued existence becomes good overall, the original deprivation remains evidence requiring an independent permission condition. This strengthens the suffering objection without asserting that restoration is conceptually impossible: the point is that compensation and justification answer different moral questions, and the former does not automatically supply the latter.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that the combined explanatory demands presented by contingent existence, apparently objective normativity, and carefully filtered religious experience make a necessary, non-arbitrary transcendent ground a reasonable cumulative inference.
premises: Contingent reality remains explanatorily incomplete if every member and every derivative structure depends upon conditions that never contain the sufficient basis of actuality within themselves.

A terminus of explanation need not be analytically defined into existence; it may instead be inferred posteriorly as nonderivative if dependent reality genuinely requires an ultimate explanatory ground.
Moral criticism presupposes standards that can correct individual feeling and prevailing custom, even though that fact alone does not yet identify those standards with a personal deity.

Religious experience gains evidential significance only when assessed cumulatively for coherence, independence, lasting transformation, cross-contextual recurrence, and comparative resistance to ordinary psychological explanations.

If one hypothesis economically explains dependent actuality, objective normative authority, and the best-filtered transcendent experiences together, its cross-domain unification can provide support exceeding any isolated argument.
finalArgument.conclusion: Accordingly, a necessary and normatively adequate transcendent ground may be affirmed as the best cumulative explanation if its unified explanatory gain exceeds the strongest naturalistic alternatives, though further argument is required to identify that ground fully with God.

newArguments.title: Cross-domain explanatory convergence
newArguments.text: The contingency, experiential, and moral routes should be evaluated as partially independent evidence rather than as three demonstrations. A necessary ground addresses why derivative reality exists; a normatively adequate ground addresses why moral criticism can outrun feeling and custom; and a transcendent personal dimension can help explain a carefully filtered class of religious experiences. If one hypothesis predicts these domains with fewer independent assumptions than rival packages, their convergence supplies additional support. This is an abductive comparison, so its force depends on specifying naturalistic competitors and measuring explanatory cost rather than merely repeating that God explains everything.

newArguments.title: Normative authority without arbitrary command
newArguments.text: The moral argument can avoid arbitrary divine command by treating goodness as grounded in the stable character of a necessarily good source, while obligations arise from reasons responsive agents have in relation to that good. This account must still compete with secular moral realism, but it explains why obligation can be objective, action-guiding, and resistant to social approval without making goodness whatever a commander happens to decree. The proposal repairs the gap between an objective criterion and God by adding an account of non-arbitrary authority, though it remains a comparative metaphysical hypothesis rather than a direct proof.

finalArgument.thesis: The AI steelman is that none of the three domains establishes God because each inference remains underdetermined once modal alternatives, evidential parity, and distinct naturalistic accounts of moral psychology and normativity are separated carefully.
premises: Explanations of contingent members do not entail that their totality has a further explanation, and any generalized principle of sufficient reason requires an independent defense rather than intuitive repetition.
Even if dependent reality has an ultimate explanation, additional premises are needed to establish that its terminus is necessary, personal, morally perfect, or appropriately identifiable as God.
Private experiences support their interpreted objects only to the extent that publicly assessable features discriminate among incompatible religious, psychological, and cultural explanations.

Historical variation and social formation can explain why moral attitudes and obligation-feelings differ, but those genealogies must be distinguished from the separate philosophical question of normative validity.
Objective moral criticism can be grounded in natural facts about agency, reciprocal justification, suffering, and coherent practical reasons without invoking either raw feeling or divine command.
finalArgument.conclusion: Therefore, withholding assent to God’s existence is reasonable unless the affirmative case independently defends sufficient reason, supplies discriminatory experiential evidence, and shows that divine grounding explains normative authority better than developed secular alternatives.

newArguments.title: The identification gap
newArguments.text: Suppose for argument’s sake that contingent reality has an ultimate nonderivative explanation. That concession does not identify the terminus as conscious, singular, morally perfect, loving, or worthy of worship. Each attribute requires a separate bridge, and some may fit impersonal laws, modal structure, or an unknown metaphysical basis equally well. The affirmative case therefore faces an identification gap after the contingency inference, not merely before it. This argument does not claim that a divine terminus is impossible; it shows that establishing an ultimate ground and establishing God are distinct explanatory achievements whose evidential requirements cannot be merged silently.

newArguments.title: Publicly corrigible experience
newArguments.text: Religious experiences may be sincere and personally significant while remaining weak public evidence when their interpretations diverge and lack independent correction procedures. A responsible evidential framework should ask whether predictions, intersubjective checks, or independently confirmed information distinguish transcendent contact from expectation, culture, neurological variation, and memory reconstruction. Transformative benefit can raise practical importance without settling ontology because fictional or mistaken beliefs may also reorganize conduct. This framework improves the skeptical case by specifying what stronger evidence would look like, thereby avoiding the crude inference that an experience is evidentially worthless merely because it is private.

newArguments.title: Secular reasons for moral correction
newArguments.text: A naturalistic account need not reduce morality to immediate feeling or inherited taboo. Agents can criticize customs by asking whether principles are coherent, reciprocally justifiable, informed by relevant facts, and responsive to suffering, autonomy, and the conditions of cooperative agency. These standards remain revisable, yet revision does not make them arbitrary any more than revisable scientific methods become mere preference. Such an account answers Copleston’s strongest criticism by explaining how socially formed people can condemn their own society without invoking a transcendent lawgiver. Its remaining burden is to defend why these practical reasons possess authority across divergent agents.

Exactly two substantive advocates carry the motion. The recording has formal rounds, so no team or moderator-advocacy exception is used. The anonymous timekeeper’s interjections are logistical. Any remaining uncertainty that is material to a selected claim must trigger below-high attribution and required audio verification; do not hide it behind a blanket caption caveat.

1. Preserve the stated question byte-for-byte. Both speakers accept textual variation. Ehrman argues that surviving copies sometimes change important wording and that recovering an early common ancestor does not guarantee every original word. Do not turn White into an advocate of perfect individual copies or Ehrman into an advocate that nothing historical can be known. 4. White explicitly compares representative PRINTED editions, not individual manuscripts, at 43:19 and in rebuttal.
